GC-21 class fix in internal/filter/validation/jsonschema (parts 1, 2 and 4 of the audit's fix; part 3, closing the routes, is GC-01/GC-02's, groups G02/G03).
(1) inspect.go: inspector.visit now calls refuseAssertions, which refuses RZ-CFG-005 at the keyword pointer whenever the compiled graph holds a schema whose Format, ContentEncoding, ContentMediaType or ContentSchema is set. For format the message is "format is an annotation, but this schema's dialect asserts it (the format-assertion vocabulary); $schema must be <Draft>". For the content keywords it is "<kw> is an annotation, but the library compiled it as an assertion". The content check is a backstop, because AssertContent is never set. Every document this refuses already carries a $schema other than Draft, so 07 req 75 forbids it today and this adds no new refusal.
(2) schema.go: regexpCache (a bare map) is replaced by regexpEngine. Each compile gets its own engine, with a cache map, a frozen flag and an atomic calls counter. compileWith and compileWalked freeze it on every return path: walk refusal, library refusal, checkApart refusal, inspector refusal, analysis refusal, the two stop points, and success. Freezing drops the cache. After that every call returns errEngineFrozen and compiles and caches nothing; the only write it makes is the atomic count. As a result no compiled Schema can reach a cache map, and a frozen engine called from concurrent requests can neither crash the process nor grow. checkApart shares the same engine, and its meta-schema is discarded before the freeze. compilePrepared, compileWith and compileWalked now take the engine as a seam, and the three existing compileWalked call sites in tests were updated.
(4) doc.go now says format and content are annotations because the compile refuses an asserted one in the compiled graph, and no longer only because the AssertFormat and AssertContent flags are unset. The concurrency paragraph says the engine is frozen and never compiles at validation. regexpCache was renamed regexpEngine in doc.go and patternsize.go. working.go notes that its Format and content error-unit terms are never set in the graph the analysis walks.
Class members fixed together: format asserted under a root $vocabulary on both library-only routes ($recursiveRef target and base-mismatch target), for each of the 6 probed formats and in a subschema of the resource; the bundled meta/format-assertion on both routes; injected Format at the root, in a member and behind a reference; each content keyword, plus all four at once; every compile-outcome path freezing the engine; the checkApart meta compiler's use of the engine; request-time calls from 8 goroutines; and the FuzzCompileSchema properties (engine frozen after compile, never called during validation).
Other path found that shares the root cause, handed to G03 (GC-02). A $dynamicAnchor schema of a library-only resource, reached only through dynamic scope, is compiled by the library (compiler.go:223-236) but is reachable through no exported edge, so the inspector never visits it, and neither does the analysis (newEvalGraph). Example: {<root $vocabulary with format-assertion>,"$recursiveRef":"#/x","x":{"$id":"urn:x","$schema":"https://schema.ruralz.invalid/policy.json","$defs":{"d":{"$dynamicAnchor":"n","format":"email"}},"$ref":"urn:y"},"$defs":{"y":{"$id":"urn:y","$dynamicAnchor":"n","properties":{"a":{"$dynamicRef":"#n"}}}}}. It compiles, and {"a":"not an email"} gets a 400. On that route this pass closes the crash and the cache growth: with format 'regex' the frozen engine fails closed (TestHandleDynamicScopeFormat). Other formats are still asserted there, and their work stays uncharged, until G03 makes those positions walked-live starts. That same change also lets GC-02's walked-live Location backstop see them. TestHandleDynamicScopeFormat passes if the compile refuses the route at $schema, so it keeps passing after G02/G03. TestFormatAssertionRefused accepts the first finding either at the format keyword or at the resource's $schema, so it too passes before and after G02/G03.
Still open, with GC-01/GC-02 per the audit's Also-needs column: the CC-04 part where a dialect's vocabulary subset drops the validation and applicator keywords on a library-only route that has no format keyword.
Fuzzing also found a pre-existing GC-01 finding: {"$recursiveRef":"0"} makes the compile ask the loader for https://schema.ruralz.invalid/0. It is present at e1e9657 (overlay probe) and matches rows CMP-35/REFS-12, owned by G02.

G02 (GC-01) check. Verdict: fix, with 3 minor findings. The code fix itself is sound. All three findings are about tests and comments.

What holds:
- **Code read.** $recursiveRef is in a shared reference-keyword list. That list feeds the walk's sites, follow, checkRef, targets/checkOrder, uncheckedPositions and loadIssues, plus inspect edges and isReference. Its order matches the library's enqueueRef call sites (objcompiler.go:90, 269, 319). Those are the only three in v6.0.3; vocab.go's Enqueue has no registered vocabulary.
- **RecursiveAnchor backstop.** The inspector refuses any compiled schema with RecursiveAnchor true.
- **Dynamic-scope charge.** flags.dynamic no longer charges $recursiveRef for walking the whole dynamic scope. The library resolves it dynamically only for a target with $recursiveAnchor true (validator.go:795-799).
- **Other backstops.** literalWork and boundWork (equal to the old charges in range), the unwalked backstop and compileWith's recover are all in place.
- **Hostile inputs.** Every input below went through compile, CompileSchema, Check and Factory.Build (probe zz_g02chk_test.go). Each ended in RZ-CFG-005 with no panic and no loader call. Each also failed on the pre-fix overlay.

    - Seven 400-repeat patterns took 329 ms and 187 MB; now 2.2 ms and 1.2 MB.
    - allOf of 40,000 took 19.7 s and 346 MB; now 25 ms.
    - The https and file references reached the loader with the finding at the root; they are now refused at /$recursiveRef.
    - multipleOf 0 below additionalItems compiled before; it is now refused.
  - Rows VLU-16, VLU-51 and VLU-52: the 20 x 1e999999 shape now allocates 41 KB, deterministic over 3 runs, against 530 ms and 55 MB pre-fix.
  - Rows CMP-31, CMP-35, REFS-13, REFS-15, REFS-25, REFS-31, CX-04 and CC-05. Base-mismatch routes carrying $recursiveAnchor are refused too.
  - Index aliases (00, +0, -0) and percent-encoded pointers still compile, so no new refusal there.

- **Checks, all pass:**

These cover the walk site list, checkRef, follow, targets, inert targets and inert sites, the inspect edge, compiledReference, the RecursiveAnchor refusal, the dynamic flag, the work edge (K09 crashes the full binary; on its own tests TestInPlaceCycles, TestWorkCharges, TestRecursiveRefTwins and TestRecursiveRefCharges kill it), the keyword and cond units, isReference, literalWork, boundWork, its denominator check, pastBound, the exponent cap, minimum and exclusiveMaximum dropped from the bound loop, unwalked nil/inert/top-most, the recover, and both extra-start variants. - heapMeter: each mark runs two collections, then reads HeapAlloc. The two collections empty sync.Pool's primary and victim caches, so pooled decoders and regexp matchers are not counted. That keeps it deterministic under -race too, where Put drops items at random.
- Marks are taken at fixed points in the code path, not on a timer:

result.summary:
Verdict: fix. I found two open problems in G04 (GC-08) and one cosmetic one.

**What I confirmed.** The sampled peakHeap, gcSlack and liveProbe are gone. All 11 tests that sampled the heap, plus decisionTree and locationTree, now use the live-heap meter (heapMeter).
- The round-9 failures are real: the old-binary logs show 1.61, 1.62 and 2.29 times the charge under load.
- I reran four of the engineer's mutants; all were killed:
  - P01 kills the chain/branch rows and the unevaluated-memory tests.
  - P04 kills TestHandleBacktrackCharge and the long sign-up row.
  - P11 kills 6 TestHandleMeasuredFit rows, TestHandleReservesDecodedMaps, TestTinyBlocks and TestPathStates.
  - H03 kills 28 rows plus 3 Handle tests.
- The tiny-block model holds:
  - An exhaustive search of the allocator's states gives a minimum block fill of 8 bytes (6 if 1-byte allocations existed).
  - mallocgcTiny and the static one-byte string match in go1.26.8 and go1.27.1.
  - Only 64-bit targets are built.
- No under-charge exists when marks are spread over the whole pass:
  - No stride peak exceeds its charge in any workingSetCases row.
  - A geometric-mark meter passed all 11 memory tests, with Handle-test peaks within 1% of the head meter's.
- doc.go's reservation-to-peak ratios match the measured values.

**Checks on the current tree:**
- go build, go vet, `golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `golangci-lint fmt --diff` (clean) and repocheck all pass.
- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1`: ok in 79 s.
- The go1.26.8 floor run: ok in 81 s.
- `go test -race -count=1 -cover -shuffle=on`: ok in 506 s, 98.2% coverage.
- All 4 fuzz targets passed 60 s each. They ran in a scratch copy of testdata, so nothing was written to the repository.

**Open findings:**
1. **Blocker.** The new TestTinyBlocks fails under load, which is exactly the defect this class removes. Its margins are 256 bytes and 1 KiB, smaller than the unrelated heap noise between two measurements (seen at 336 bytes and up to 5.5 KB). It failed in 1 of 18 memory-test process-runs and in 2 of 180 TestTinyBlocks-only runs, on both toolchains. So the class acceptance run does not hold.
2. **Major.** For failing bodies, the meter never marks the decision pass at its peak, which comes at the end of the pass. The library does call the probe there, after the oneOf, anyOf or allOf has failed and inside propertyNames checks, but the meter only marks the first 8 calls and the root. The decision check reads about 0 against a real 0.55 to 0.86 of the charge on 7 rows (0.03 to 0.34 on two more). Three comments say the decision pass reaches no probe after a failure, which is false. doc.go's "within 0.67 (decision)" figure is wrong; the measured peak reaches 0.86. The mutant decideMemory = max(decide, path) + transient survives the full suite.
3. **Minor.** Mid-sentence line breaks in comments at meter_test.go:141 and :346 and doc.go:600-603.

I changed no repository file. Probes, mutants and outputs are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp51close/g04check/.

G04 (GC-08) attempt 2 closes the check's blocker, its major and its minor. Production code is unchanged: doc.go and patternsize.go changed in comments only. Every class member was tested and proved.

BLOCKER: live-heap comparisons depended on load. TestTinyBlocks no longer compares a raw live-heap growth with the charge. tinyCensus builds 60,000 strings as the decoder does, with the collector off, then runs three checks:
(a) Model. The charge covers the replica's blocks except the current one. This check is exact.
(b) Allocator. The real allocator's 16-byte blocks are counted by address (reflect.Value.Pointer) and must equal the replica's within tinyApart = 8. All 23 sequences measured 0 apart. One-byte strings must share their one static byte.
(c) Heap. The live-heap growth stays within 16 x blocks + heapNoise.

I found the noise sources with a heap-profile probe: 9,000 measurements beside busy loops, on both toolchains.
- A new thread keeps 5,312 bytes (m 2,048, profiling stacks 2,304, two goroutine records of 480).
- GC workers cache semaphore records of 112 bytes each.
- A freed record cache shows as -7.2 KB.
These explain the check's 336 B and 5.3 to 5.5 KB readings. heapNoise is 16 KiB, which allows three threads.

The class is every exact comparison of a measured figure with a charge. All of them now go through exceeds() (charge + heapNoise) or use treeSlack (64 KiB, which now documents that it covers noise):
- TestTinyBlocks;
- the decoded-tree comparisons in TestHandleMeasuredFit and TestHandleReservesDecodedMaps (headrooms 10,198 and 16,720 bytes);
- peak against reserved in TestHandleMeasuredFit, TestHandlePatternFit, TestHandleBacktrackCharge, TestHandleReservesDecodedMaps, TestHandleBoundsUnevaluatedMemory, TestHandleUnevaluatedBranches, TestHandleBoundsMatchedItems, TestHandleBoundsValidationMemory and TestPathStates.
Members of the same class, also fixed:
- meteredPattern's exact replica check: allocations can only gain noise, so a match is measured up to 3 times and the fewest allocations are used.
- locationTree's base held the caller's Schema, which can die before the mark (-5.9 MB, hidden by peak's clamp at 0): it now keeps s live and returns the raw growth.
- decisionTree returns the raw growth at the end mark.
- tinyCensus keeps sizes and src live.
